E1 discusses hot cracking in CoCrFeNiCu, E2 suggests >600°C preheating for a different refractory HEA (WMoTaNbV), and E3 notes vertical cracks without preheating in an unspecified material. None of the cited passages provide evidence on AlCrFeNiSi's behavior, the effect of preheating on its segregation or mechanical properties, or the specific 600°C target.
premises: Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients and cooling rates in L-PBF.
Reduced cooling rates enhance diffusion-mediated homogenization, mitigating microsegregation.
Reduced thermal gradients lower residual thermal stresses and suppress hot cracking.
Preheating at ~600°C is effective for crack-free processing of refractory HEAs.
L-PBF without preheating leads to vertical cracks due to high cooling rates and thermal gradients.
